verdict.rationale: First-party docs reference an on-premises SharePoint 2016-or-later edition alongside SharePoint Online. Community reports describe running SharePoint on a single server or a server farm, and keeping a separate installation, which corroborates that it can be self-hosted. However, the evidence is only a passing mention in REST docs, not dedicated self-hosting guidance. Commenters also report heavy operational burden: farms beyond about two dozen users, frequent patching and complicated restores. Missing for 10: first-party installation/deployment documentation, version-support or licensing details for on-prem, and evidence that current features (e.g., Copilot/SPFx Online-only items) are available when self-hosted.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: The SharePoint Online (and on-premises SharePoint 2016 or later) REST service supports combining multiple requests into a single call to the service
SharePoint is usable on a single server with a small workgroup. Beyond about two dozen people, it needs a server farm
they set that installation up entirely separate from other instances on the network
